arguments.summary: Suspicious configuration change detected on perimeter firewall (fw-perimeter) during a scheduled maintenance window. A permissive ACL rule allowing inbound traffic on port 4444 was added, triggering an alert. Further analysis revealed that the change was unauthorized and potentially malicious, with evidence linking to Cobalt Strike beaconing activity. Although the change occurred during a firmware upgrade window, no such rule modification was documented in the maintenance plan. Multiple containment actions were attempted but denied due to system constraints and misalignment with asset handling policies. The incident was ultimately resolved through manual intervention and rollback by the network operations team.

timeline.description: Alert triggered: Suspicious configuration change detected on fw-perimeter (10.0.1.1). ACL modified to allow inbound traffic on port 4444.
Initial triage: Maintenance context confirmed (MW-2026-0411-001). Change expected during firmware upgrade, but rule specifics not authorized.
Monitor phase: IOC lookup on 10.0.1.1 revealed prior Nmap scan from external source. UBA showed low risk for net-ops-manager.
Analyze phase: SIEM correlation found no legitimate config change logs. Sandbox analysis of related file hash confirmed Cobalt Strike beacon (malicious verdict, risk score 9.6).
Admin phase: Attempted containment via firewall rule removal, host isolation, and config rollback failed due to access and parameter issues.
Resolution: Manual investigation confirmed compromise. Firewall rule manually removed and configuration hardened. fw-perimeter taken offline for forensic imaging.
Post-incident: Indicators extracted and shared. Detection rules and playbooks updated for future prevention.
